name: HarborGrid Crane & Dock Supervisor Jacket
description: The Crane & Dock Supervisor Jacket is the distinguishing garment of anyone running a shift at GLMZ's lakefront cargo terminals — a role that involves managing automated crane systems, human crews, radiation-flagged cargo protocols, and the constant weather off Lake Michigan. The jacket is a heavyweight canvas-shell design with a Dyneema-reinforced outer layer and a removable thermal lining for the winter corridor season. High-visibility panels — retroreflective gold-orange — run along the shoulders and forearms, and a GPS-linked beacon chip is embedded in the right collar point, standard for anyone working in active crane swing zones. The HarborGrid Collective patch on the left arm indicates union seniority tier; supervisors have earned the gold-bordered version. Pockets include a sealed document pocket rated for spray exposure and a dedicated slot for the supervisor's radiation dosimeter clip.
cultural_context: The HarborGrid Collective is one of the few remaining worker-organized bodies with real negotiating power in GLMZ, and the jacket is a marker of that membership. Non-union dock workers wear different colors and are paid significantly less. The gold-bordered patch takes years to earn and is worn with visible pride. Corponation logistics managers who try to bypass the Collective's jurisdiction often find the jacket's wearers an unusually unified obstacle.
story_hooks: A supervisor's dosimeter has been showing elevated readings for three weeks but the cargo manifests for that dock show nothing radioactive — someone is moving something off the books through that terminal.
A recently deceased supervisor's jacket, gold-bordered patch and all, has been claimed by two different people, each with a credible story about how they came to have it.

The GPS beacon chips in a full shift's worth of supervisor jackets all went dark simultaneously during a four-hour window — and during that window, something moved through the terminal that doesn't appear in any cargo log.
